newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses drive higher, rate fears linger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses drive higher, rate fears linger.

text.p: European stocks strengthened on Monday following Wall Street's good showing on Friday but worries about a possible U.S. rate rise continued to linger.
German shares rose more than one percent in early trade, while Britain's blue-chip FTSE 100 index drove back above 3,900 to within a few points of its record high.
An attempt by the dollar to test higher levels tailed off in European morning business but traders said it looked well supported whenever it dipped.
By 0930 GMT the dollar was at 1.4916 marks and 109.03 yen, compared with 1.4913 and 109.32 in late European trade on Friday.
Financial markets remained gripped by interest rate prospects following last Friday's U.S. jobs data showing lower unemployment and stronger earnings in August.
"It has helped to give the U.S. asset markets a firmer underlying tone and that tends to help the dollar," said Alex Jackson, manager treasury sales at Nikko Bank in London.
Many traders and investors are betting on a rise of 0.25 percentage point in U.S. interest rates when the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
"It's pretty clear the Fed will raise rates. The debate is simply about when and how much," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
Any rise should help the dollar higher but would weigh on stock markets around the world as investors may be tempted to switch out of equities into bonds.
British stocks bounced higher at the start of trading and got another boost from producer price figures showing output prices rose 1.2 percent year-on-year, the lowest rise since October 1967.
"Excellent figures, particularly impressive when you bear in mind several adverse factors, notably the rise in global oil prices," Mark Hale of Sakura Finance commented.
British government bonds firmed following the prices data and stocks drove within 11 points of their trading record of 3,922.1 set on August 28.
By 0930 GMT the FTSE index was trading around its high for the day of 3,911, up 18 points from Friday's close.
Some traders saw the gains being capped by persistent fears that the United States will raise rates to cool growth and Wall Street's volatile reaction to the jobs data.
German shares responded to a late burst of buying on Friday by pushing the 30-share DAX index up by more than one percent in early trade.
Traders said they expected trading to remain limited to a tight range until volume picked up, however.
Volkswagen shares rose after VW chief Ferdinand Piech said in a weekend interview he planned to boost the car-maker's return on sales more than tenfold by the end of the century.
In Paris stocks opened higher, too, buoyed 10 points by rising bond prices and favourable first-half company results, brokers said.
Shares in holding company Cerus rallied 12 percent after being suspended twice, limit-up, on a newspaper report that it was negotiating a possible buyout by CGIP.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4916 marks and 109.03 yen, compared with 1.4913 marks and 109.32 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was up 18.1 points at 3,911.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 30.59 at 2,547.59.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 10.56 at 2,015.31
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $385 an ounce in the morning, against a $385.55 close in London on Friday. Silver,trendless and following gold, began two cents down at $5.13.
